project.name: Boarhills
project.boundarySource: Resolved named-place location with a conservative strict settlement study buffer
project.researchNotes: Sequential place 9 of 13: every visitor category, strict boundary, all four named trail providers, local HES/NRHE completeness, construction dates, access, transport and dogs were rechecked before continuing. Doors Open refreshments, toilets and event parking are not dependable daily facilities. Cambo, Kingsbarns and St Andrews services are not transferred.

touristAppeal.label: Limited Visitor Interest
touristAppeal.summary: Boarhills offers a restored doocot green, picnic tables, community walking leaflets and access to the Fife Coastal Path, but lacks a qualifying café, dependable general visitor parking and public toilets. It is a worthwhile short stop, not a rounded 60+ town destination.
touristAppeal.dogAccessSummary: The community green and walking routes support an outdoor dog visit; close control is essential around farmland, wildlife, roads and any golf crossing.

visitorHighlights.name: Boarhills Doocot and Community Green
visitorHighlights.reason: A genuinely public, restored and interpreted heritage stop directly beside a major trail, but modest in scale and without dependable indoor opening.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Open-air community green with free access

townGuide.characterTag: Rural village, doocot green and coast-path hub
townGuide.headline: Worth a short trail stop, not a standalone day out
townGuide.intro: Boarhills offers a restored doocot green, picnic tables, community walking leaflets and access to the Fife Coastal Path, but lacks a qualifying café, dependable general visitor parking and public toilets. It is a worthwhile short stop, not a rounded 60+ town destination.
perfectFor: A pause while walking the coast path

suggestedFirstVisit.title: Doocot and community green
suggestedFirstVisit.summary: Use the community green as a short heritage and picnic pause; plan any longer walk from the official coastal-path page.

townGuide.visitorMood: Quiet rural heritage beside a major path.

features.name: Kenlygreen House
features.fullDescription: Late 18th century, partly restored. Main block 2-storey 5-window channelled pilasters centre and ends with urns over, slightly later R-doric pilastered and pedimented porch; slated piend roof, twin chimneys each gable; single storey 1-window pedimented wings with channelled pilasters and urns at apices; short set back links with (modern) elliptical windows. White lined out stucco with ashlar dressings, all windows to front architraved.
